findings.title: Dev mode now serializes every request behind a write lock held across file and network I/O
findings.body: In dev mode the condition `cfg.Env != setting.Dev && ret != nil` is always false, so every call falls through to `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` and holds the exclusive lock for the whole reload. That reload can call `readWebAssetsFromCDN` (an HTTP request made with `http.DefaultClient`, which has no timeout) and then read and parse the manifest from disk. Before this change, concurrent dev-mode requests ran in parallel. Now they queue behind one another, and a slow CDN response stalls every caller, including ones that only need the read path. Waiting callers also ignore their own `ctx` cancellation while blocked on the lock. Consider doing the reload outside the lock, or only holding the lock while publishing the result.

findings.title: No double-checked read after acquiring the write lock, so concurrent cold-start callers each reload the manifest
findings.body: The RLock check at lines 41-47 happens once, and the write lock is taken at line 48 without re-checking the cache. If several goroutines miss the cache at the same time, they each acquire the write lock in turn and each re-read the manifest file (and possibly the CDN) even though the first one has already populated `entryPointAssetsCache`. Re-checking `cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil` after `Lock()` would avoid the redundant work in non-dev mode.

findings.title: Data race fix has no regression test
findings.body: The PR fixes a data race on the package-level `entryPointAssetsCache`, but no test is added or changed. A test that calls `GetWebAssets` concurrently from multiple goroutines (in both dev and non-dev environments, run under `go test -race`) would confirm the fix and keep the race from coming back. Without it, nothing in CI exercises the locking path.
